chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 1.1
chunks.content: Symptom: Fan not working. Possible cause and actions: The main switch is open. The manual lists closing the switch as the corrective action. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 1.1. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 1.4
chunks.content: Symptom: Fan not working. Possible cause and actions: The unit may be in its defrost cycle. Wait for that cycle to finish. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 1.4. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 1.7
chunks.content: Symptom: Fan not working. Possible cause and actions: Ice or debris may obstruct the fan. The manual lists removing obstructions and checking the fan junction box for a short circuit. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 1.7. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.1
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: The room thermostat may be set too high. Reduce the thermostat setting. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.1. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.3
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: The refrigeration system may be low on refrigerant. The manual lists checking for leaks and adding refrigerant. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.3. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.4
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: Ice may be blocking the coil. Manually defrost the coil and check the defrost system. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.4. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.5
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: The cooler may be too close to a door. The manual suggests moving the unit or adding a strip curtain or air curtain at the door. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.5. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.6
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: Too much air may enter through open doors. Check the door seals and replace them if needed. Keep doors shut for as much of the time as possible. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.6. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.7
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: Products may have just been put into the cold room. Wait for those products to cool down. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.7. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 2.8
chunks.content: Symptom: Room temperature too high. Possible cause and actions: The refrigeration system may be switched off. The listed action is to switch the system on. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 2.8. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 3.1
chunks.content: Symptom: Ice on the ceiling or fan. Possible cause and actions: The defrost cycle may run too long. Shorten the defrost cycle. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 3.1. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 4.4
chunks.content: Symptom: Coil still frosted after defrost. Possible cause and actions: The defrost cycle may be too short. Increase its duration using the defrost thermostat or timer. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 4.4. Teaching paraphrase.

chunks.title: Optyma Cooler · p. 6 · entry 5.3
chunks.content: Symptom: Uneven coil frosting. Possible cause and actions: The time allowed for dripping after defrost may be too short. Increase that time. Source: Danfoss Optyma Cooler, page 6, section 13, entry 5.3. Teaching paraphrase.
